issues.title: Transpose orientation in the OSI–FFPI equivalence induction
issues.failure_explanation: The proposition asserts A_t = P_t bar(A_t) Q_t^top. Hence bar(A_t) = P_t^top A_t Q_t, so its left Gramian equals P_t^top(sum_i A_{t,i}A_{t,i}^top)P_t. The old proof instead uses P_t(sum_i A_{t,i}A_{t,i}^top)P_t^top. Assumption 1 and orthogonality do not imply P_t = P_t^top or the required commutation, and arbitrary factor choices can produce nonsymmetric orthogonal P_t. Consequently the ensuing identity P_t L_t C_t = bar(C_t)P_{t+1}^top and the old L-update do not follow.
issues.overall_effect: The written induction does not establish the proposition's claimed orthogonal equivalence between OSI and factor fixed-point iterates. The later formal convergence results analyze the fixed-point maps independently, so no later formal result is identified as dependent on this erroneous orientation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the induction step from the equivalent relation \(\bar{\mathbf A}_t=P_t^\top\mathbf A_tQ_t\). Thus its left Gramian is \(P_t^\top(\sum_i A_{t,i}A_{t,i}^\top)P_t\), giving \(P_t^\top L_tC_t=\bar C_tP_{t+1}^\top\) and hence \(L_{t+1}=P_{t+1}\bar L_{t+1}P_t^\top L_t\). Propagate these transpose orientations through the remaining left-factor calculation and the final induction identity; the right-factor argument then completes the proposition unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes an invalid congruence transformation, so this is not merely transcriptional: several ensuing identities must be corrected. Nevertheless, the proposition itself uniquely supplies the proper orientation, and a short, routine local matrix-algebra correction repairs the entire induction without a new lemma, changed hypotheses, weakened conclusion, or effect on any dependent formal result.
